segments.label: live-pin-rule-for-tests · cc:-home-joe-code-voxterm · said 2026-09-02
segments.text:
**Why:** authored constants encode the author's assumed vocabulary; the live path's vocabulary drifts (type, shape, presence) without failing such tests.
A test whose fixtures speak a vocabulary the live path doesn't speak stays green while meaning something false. Two same-evening instances (2026-09-02, futon2/futon3c): the U8 report gate's `:u8/mission-status-signal-overbroad` kept firing (test green) after D11 removed the overbroad condition — it was now firing on a typed *absence*; and the wm side's `mission_c_test` pinned a Bernoulli branch with a long `0` that the live all-doubles observation vocabulary can never produce, so `(= 0 x)` was false live while the test passed.
**How to apply:** when writing or reviewing a test packet, require at least one pin whose values are captured verbatim from a live record (id cited) — e.g. D11's negative tests quote the actual false-positive prose from the store. In review, ask of every green test: *which live record does this agree with?* Corollary (same class, same evening): any claim of the form "all sites are X" must state the search command and whether its output was truncated — a head-limited grep presented as an enumeration is the tool speaking a truncated vocabulary while the text stays confident. Second corollary (2026-09-02, SURPRISES entry 9 correction 7ad831a): reproduction validates numbers, not their labels — a review-confirmed, byte-reproduced measurement can still mis-attribute its population ("live decisions" that were actually calibration sessions); check what the counted things ARE, not only that the counts re-derive. Adopted in the zaif-harness board conventions (futon2/holes/labs/zaif-harness/work
Require at least one test pin captured verbatim from a live record; tests built only from authored constants can stay green while meaning something false

segments.label: park-deadlines-budget-the-acceptance-run · cc:-home-joe-code-voxterm · said 2026-09-02
segments.text:
"Park deadlines must cover the acceptance runs a packet demands, not just the coding time"
**How to apply:** when writing the packet, add up what the acceptance bar makes the agent *run*, and set `--park-deadline` to comfortably exceed coding plus that. If the bar includes a command you have timed yourself, use the measured number. See [[never-amend-in-shared-futon-trees]].
**Why:** a deadline wake that fires on a job which is merely slow, not stuck, costs a round of "is it healthy?" reasoning and can trigger a needless re-dispatch. The park exists to catch silence, not to race the acceptance bar.
CLAUDE.md sets a floor of 45 min for Codex park deadlines. That floor is about the *coding*; it is not enough when the packet's own acceptance bar requires long verification runs. On 2026-09-02 claude-6 belled a packet whose acceptance demanded two ~10-minute `wm_status_report.py` runs (each launches two bounded test suites), parked at 2700s, and the deadline fired at 18:17 while the job sat in `delivering` — it had finished at 18:16:47. A third of the budget was verification, not work.

segments.label: never-git-stash-in-shared-futon-trees · cc:-home-joe-code-voxterm · said 2026-09-09
segments.text:
"Never `git stash` in a shared futon tree; a no-op stash push followed by pop applies a stranger's old stash entry. Use `git show <sha>^:<path> > <path>` to test pre-fix code."
**How to apply:** to run tests against pre-fix code, check the old blob out by path instead — `git show <sha>^:<path> > <path>`, run, then `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`. It touches only the file you named and cannot reach the stash stack. Verify with `git status --porcelain` afterwards. If a pop does fire, `git restore --staged --worktree <paths>` returns them to HEAD and leaves the stash entries intact — do not drop them, they are not yours. See [[never-amend-in-shared-futon-trees]], whose "commit or stash them" advice does not extend to popping in a shared tree.
**Why:** stash is a stack shared with every other agent working the tree, and its push is silently a no-op when the path is already committed — which is exactly the state right after you commit a review fix.
On 2026-09-09 that put conflict markers into `holes/labs/M-apm-demonstration/frame-park-decisions.edn`. The APM coordinator reads that file every tick, so within about a minute the jit-all-open-v3 regulator went `:failed` with `:problem-queue-park-decision-read-failed` ("Map literal must contain an even number of forms") and the campaign stopped until the file was restored and the coordinator resumed.
The shared futon repos carry other agents' abandoned stash entries — futon3c has two from 2026-09-01 (`codex/http-test-ledger-isolation`, `codex/persona-registry-aliases`). `git stash push -q <path>` on a **clean** path creates no entry and says nothing under `-q`, so the following `git stash pop` pops whichever stranger's entry is on top and applies it to the shared tree.

segments.label: shared-worktree-never-commit-a · cc:-home-joe-code · said 2026-10-04
segments.text:
2026-08-22, `git commit -qam` (futon3c a2af5067) silently included codex-13's half-finished `agent_pouch.clj` / `http.clj`; the Codex bellback then cited *my* sha as its implementation commit. Not rewritten — the mislabelled commit stands.
2026-09-05, working row :F6 in futon2 I committed `20381c6c`, then spent a few minutes on a one-line comment fix and ran `git commit --amend --no-edit`. The library-loop lane had committed `d3c36581` in between, so the amend rewrote *their* commit (`1ac01e5e`), pulling my generator file into it. Repaired with `git reset --soft d3c36581` (the pre-amend sha from `git reflog`), then a fresh commit of my own — their commit is byte-identical again.
**Why (two incidents, same root: HEAD is not yours):**
2026-10-04, mfuton-sbcl. My new `tools/smoke.sh` ended with `git checkout -- lisp/transpiler/evidence` "to drop test churn". Run once in the shared checkout, it discarded ~22 *other agents'* uncommitted receipt edits (not in git, unrecoverable). Fixed by tar-snapshot + exact restore.
shared checkouts (futon3c, futon2, mfuton-sbcl) — `git commit -a` swept in another agent's files (2026-08-22); `--amend` rewrote another lane's commit (2026-09-05); another writer committed MY staged index (2026-09-07); a script's `git checkout -- dir` discarded ~22 uncommitted receipts (2026-10-04)
**How to apply:** `git add <paths>` then `git commit`; run `git status --short` *after* the add and expect to see your paths staged — if they are missing, someone else committed them, so find the sha with `git log -1 --stat` and report **that** sha rather than assuming your commit exists. Never `--amend` without checking `git log --oneline -1` is still your commit — prefer a follow-up commit. Never put `git checkout --`/`git restore`/`git clean` of a path into a script that may run in a shared checkout; snapshot and restore the files instead. If you do amend by mistake, `git reflog` still holds the original; `git reset --soft <original-sha>` restores it with your change left staged. Also: the Agency JVM (port 7070, Drawbridge 6768) takes `(require 'ns :reload)` via `/eval` for function bodies only — new routes must go in `futon3c.transport.http/extra-routes`, `(do …)` forms are rejected by `/eval`, and `rebuild-handler!` has no builder on the zone server. See [[park-payloads-must-not-r
In any checkout other agents are also committing to (`/home/joe/code/futon3c`, `/home/joe/code/futon2`): stage exact paths, and **re-read `git log -1` right before `--amend`**.
2026-09-07, wm-edge loop row `:F12` slice 16 in futon2. I wrote three files, ran `git add <three paths>`, and the very next `git status --short` showed them *already tracked and clean*: an unidentified writer had committed them as `23f22dc5` seconds earlier, so my own `git commit` reported "nothing added to commit". Not the build loop — `wm-build-loop.sh` only commits `workflow-report.edn` and `worklist.edn`. The content was byte-identical to mine, but the sha and the commit message were someone else's.

segments.label: never-amend-in-shared-futon-trees · cc:-home-joe-code-voxterm · said 2026-09-25
segments.text:
**How to apply:** corrections are always follow-up commits. Before committing in a shared tree, check `git log -1` — if HEAD isn't yours, never amend or reset it. When reviewing a delivered sha, confirm it is still reachable from HEAD (collisions are disclosed in the lab's SURPRISES.md process section). Don't leave in-progress untracked files sitting in a shared tree — commit or stash them; a concurrent dirt review will adopt them and invent a rationale. See [[agency-dispatch-mode-work]].
**Why:** other agents report and park on shas the moment they commit; a rewrite invalidates their reports and mixes authorship in the record.
In the shared futon trees (futon2, futon3c, …) multiple agents commit to master concurrently, minutes apart. Never `git commit --amend` there: on 2026-09-02 claude-1's amend rewrote codex-22's just-landed commit (b8c4463 → 33f7a46), folding unrelated changes into another agent's commit and leaving the reported sha dangling — the second collision that evening (the first was 206bb02, a staged-files sweep). Path-scoped commits (`git commit -- <paths>`) protect what you sweep IN; amend rewrites whatever HEAD happens to be.
"Never `git commit --amend` in the shared futon repos; corrections are follow-up commits, and verify HEAD is yours before any commit"
A third variant, 2026-09-02: **untracked** in-progress files get swept too. While claude-6 was mid-review with new `test/fixtures/*` in the futon2 working tree, another lane's "dirt review" (futon2-d promotion hold) committed them as 108d9f0 with a message asserting they had been omitted from e0d1868 — false; the test that reads them was still uncommitted. Content was identical so nothing needed redoing, but the record now carries a wrong claim about another commit.
Also (2026-09-25): in a shared checkout ALWAYS commit with explicit paths, `git commit -m ... -- <paths>`, never bare `git add X && git commit`. A bare commit sweeps whatever another seat has staged: claude-8's PROOF-2a record commit 92beed80 swallowed claude-6's three staged H-VALUE-G-D files, so the packet lives in a commit whose message is about something else.

segments.label: no-git-stash-in-shared-checkout · cc:-home-joe-code · said 2026-09-30
segments.text:
never use git stash / stash pop to test against old code in a shared checkout; pop can apply someone else's old stash
**Why:** on 2026-09-30 the file was already committed, so `git stash` saved nothing, and `git stash pop` then applied a preserved stash from 2026-09-01 (codex/http-test-ledger-isolation) onto futon3c master: four live `emacs/*.el` files modified and two files left with conflicts. Recovered with `git checkout HEAD -- <the six files>`; the stash entry survived because the pop failed. See [[shared-worktree-never-commit-a]] and [[futon3c-emacs-dir-is-live-code]].
**How to apply:** to run a test against an earlier version, write it to a temp path with `git show <sha>:path > /tmp/...` and point the test at that (PYTHONPATH or a copied file), never through the stash. futon3c has two long-lived preserved stashes that must not be popped or dropped.
Do not use `git stash -- FILE; test; git stash pop` to check a test against the unfixed code in the shared futon checkouts.
